title.en: Text Generation: Teaching an RNN to Write

description.en: Build a character-level language model using an LSTM to generate text one character at a time.

story_variants.en:
## Text Generation: Teaching an RNN to Write

A character-level language model learns to predict the next character given all previous characters. Given enough training, it can generate convincing new text in the style of the training data.

### The Core Idea

```
Input:   "hell" → predict → 'o'
Input:   "hello" → predict → ' '
Input:   "hello " → predict → 'w'
```

### Building the Dataset

```python
text = "hello world"
vocab = sorted(set(text))
char2idx = {c: i for i, c in enumerate(vocab)}
idx2char = {i: c for c, i in char2idx.items()}

# Create input-target pairs (one step apart)
X = [char2idx[c] for c in text[:-1]]
Y = [char2idx[c] for c in text[1:]]
```

### The Model (PyTorch)

```python
import torch
import torch.nn as nn

class CharLM(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, vocab_size, embed_dim=32, hidden_size=128):
        super().__init__()
        self.embed   = nn.Embedding(vocab_size, embed_dim)
        self.lstm    = nn.LSTM(embed_dim, hidden_size, batch_first=True)
        self.linear  = nn.Linear(hidden_size, vocab_size)

    def forward(self, x, hidden=None):
        x = self.embed(x)
        out, hidden = self.lstm(x, hidden)
        return self.linear(out), hidden
```

### Generating Text

```python
def generate(model, seed_char, length=100, temperature=0.8):
    model.eval()
    idx = char2idx[seed_char]
    hidden = None
    result = [seed_char]
    for _ in range(length):
        x = torch.tensor([[idx]])
        logits, hidden = model(x, hidden)
        probs = torch.softmax(logits[0,-1] / temperature, dim=0)
        idx = torch.multinomial(probs, 1).item()
        result.append(idx2char[idx])
    return ''.join(result)
```

### Temperature Controls Creativity

| Temperature | Effect |
|------------|--------|
| < 0.5 | Repetitive, safe text |
| 0.8–1.0 | Balanced creativity |
| > 1.5 | Wild, incoherent text |

> **Key Concept:** Temperature divides the logits before softmax. Low temperature sharpens the distribution (model is more certain); high temperature flattens it (more random sampling).

animation_sequence.code:
import torch
import torch.nn as nn

class TextGenerator(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, vocab_size, embed_dim, hidden_dim):
        super().__init__()
        self.embed = nn.Embedding(vocab_size, embed_dim)
        self.lstm = nn.LSTM(embed_dim, hidden_dim, batch_first=True)
        self.fc = nn.Linear(hidden_dim, vocab_size)
    def forward(self, x, hidden=None):
        x = self.embed(x)
        out, hidden = self.lstm(x, hidden)
        return self.fc(out), hidden

model = TextGenerator(vocab_size=100, embed_dim=32, hidden_dim=64)
x = torch.randint(0, 100, (1, 15))
logits, hidden = model(x)
print(f'Logits: {logits.shape}')

under_the_hood.summary: A character-level model is trained to predict each next character from the ones before; to generate, it takes a seed character, turns its output scores into probabilities, samples one character, feeds it back in with the carried hidden state, and repeats.

steps.title: Text becomes index sequences
steps.body: For 'hello world', sorted(set(text)) gives 8 characters: ' ', d, e, h, l, o, r, w, numbered 0 to 7. The input is every character but the last and the target is every character but the first, so 'h' should predict 'e', 'e' should predict 'l', and so on.

props.caption: First input -> target pairs (shifted by one)

steps.title: Embedding, LSTM, scores
steps.body: nn.Embedding(8, 32) turns each index into a learned 32-number vector. The LSTM (hidden size 128) reads them in order, and a Linear(128, 8) layer turns each hidden state into 8 scores, one per character. Cross-entropy compares the scores at every position with the true next character.

steps.title: Context changes the prediction
steps.body: After 'l' the right answer is sometimes 'l' (in 'hel|lo') and sometimes 'o' (in 'hell|o'). Only the hidden state, which remembers 'he' versus 'hel', lets the model tell these apart. That is why the hidden state is carried from character to character during generation too.

steps.title: Generation is a sampling loop
steps.body: Start from a seed character with hidden = None. Each step: run the model on the last character and the current hidden state, divide the logits by the temperature, softmax them, draw one index with torch.multinomial, append its character, and use it as the next input. Repeat 100 times for 100 characters.

nodes.label: append; feed it back with new hidden

steps.title: Temperature controls risk
steps.body: Dividing logits by 0.5 doubles their gaps, so the favourite character dominates and text gets repetitive. Dividing by 1.5 shrinks the gaps, so unlikely characters appear more often and text gets creative but error-prone. At 0.8 the model mostly follows what it learned while still varying.

under_the_hood.takeaway: Training teaches next-character prediction; generation turns predictions into text by sampling and feeding each choice back. The same predict-sample-append loop, scaled up to tokens and transformers, is how today's language models write.
